top_choice_rationale: P001 credits a single sharply defined idea, the magic-wavelength optical lattice, to Katori (concept and first realisations) and Ye (the many-atom regime at 1e-18 and its use as a physics instrument), with a clean two-name allocation and independent agreement below 1e-18 across laboratories. A citation anchored on the lattice clock, with the comb and ion control only as enabling background, separates it from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P002 is a strong prediction-then-experiment story but rests on an unsettled pairing mechanism and a three-name cut that excludes Cao, Fatemi and the hBN moire groups, so I rank it second, above no award.
